newsitem.title: FRANCE: Church offers troubled Renault advice from Bible.
newsitem.headline: Church offers troubled Renault advice from Bible.

text.p: The Catholic Church said Friday that plans by carmaker Renault to shut its Belgian factory with 3,100 job losses highlighted the human cost of cut-throat economics and competition, and offered advice from the Bible.
"Treat others as you would like them to treat you," said a joint statement by the conference of French and Belgian Catholic Churches, quoting from the Gospel of Saint Luke.
The French carmaker has run into a storm of union, political -- and now religious -- controversy after announcing plans to shut the Belgian factory in a bid to become more competitive.

"An industrial group with an international presence has not been able to find a more equitable plan for its employees at the level of the European Union than the one we now know. What will be the Europe of tomorrow?" the Church statement said.

"Do we want a Europe which is testimony to the ideal of respect for the dignity of all and everyone ... You cannot pull down economic and financial borders only to put them back up again when it comes to sharing in solidarity," the statement said.

In another development, Spain Friday dropped attempts to subsidise Renault's modernisation of a Spanish plant, which the European Union opposed. European Commissioner Karel Van Miert threatened Thursday to block state subsidies to a Renault plant in Valladolid, Spain, saying it was "absurd" for the firm to close a profitable plant in Belgium while investing with government aid in Spain.
The automaker had estimated labour costs in Spain at 25 percent lower than in Belgium.
